description.narrative: The Drought Anticipatory Actions Project in Thatta, Sindh, aims to enhance community resilience and preparedness against drought by implementing a series of early interventions. The project consists of two key phases: Preparedness Activities and Anticipatory Actions, ensuring that vulnerable communities are equipped with the knowledge, resources, and response mechanisms to mitigate the impact of drought. The preparedness phase focuses on beneficiary assessment, awareness-raising sessions on water conservation and hygiene practices, and the dissemination of IEC materials to promote long-term behavioral change. Additionally, capacity-building trainings for Drought Response Teams (DRTs) and District Disaster Management Authority (DDMA) officials drought response and mitigation measure along with Mental Health & Psychosocial Support. The project will conduct coordination meetings with government authorities, will strengthen institutional response mechanisms and improve contingency planning.In the anticipatory actions phase, the project will provide multipurpose cash assistance to 500 vulnerable households, ensuring financial flexibility to meet immediate needs. To address water scarcity and hygiene concerns, 500 hygiene kits will be distributed, and clean drinking water will be provided through water tankering for two months. Recognizing the impact of drought on livestock-dependent communities, the project includes fodder distribution for 500 households’ livestock and vaccination of 500 animals with government support to prevent disease outbreaks. Additionally, a feedback and complaint mechanism will be established to ensure transparency and accountability, while post-distribution monitoring will assess the effectiveness of the interventions and inform future response strategies. Through these integrated efforts, the project aims to reduce drought-induced vulnerabilities, strengthen coping mechanisms, and support sustainable resilience-building in Thatta.
